test_title: PYST 22: Selection Post (Matric Level) - Quant (Held On 27 Jun 2023 Shift 2)
subject: maths
question: A bus is running at a speed of 60 km/h to cover a distance in 50 minutes. To reduce the time of the journey to 20 min, at what speed (in km/h) should the bus run?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time.

Time Ratio = 50 : 20 = 5 : 2

Speed Ratio = 2 : 5

Here, 2 units → 60 km/h ⇒ 1 unit → 30 km/h

New Speed = 5 units = 5 × 30 = 150 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 150 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Speed (S₁) = 60 km/h

Initial Time (T₁) = 50 min

New Time (T₂) = 20 min

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/249eeba0b5309d02768e21a545d5e1a769750485ece8111b3ed4e56221af0b15.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Since the distance covered remains the same in both cases, we can equate the distances:

S₁ × T₁ = S₂ × T₂

**Calculation:**

⇒ 60 × 50 = S₂ × 20

⇒ S₂ = (60 × 50) ÷ 20

⇒ S₂ = 3000 ÷ 20

⇒ S₂ = 150 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 150 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unit Conversions

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply the speed by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Average Speed

Average Speed is the ratio of Total Distance to Total Time. If equal distances are covered at speeds a and b, Average Speed = (2ab) ÷ (a + b).

Relative Speed

When two bodies move in the same direction, Relative Speed = |S₁ − S₂|. When moving in opposite directions, Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂.
